name: Realistic Window Replacement Timeline in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: What is a realistic installation timeline for replacing 10–20 windows in a typical Los Angeles County single-family home, from contract signing to final inspection?
mainEntity.text: What is a realistic installation timeline for replacing 10–20 windows in a typical Los Angeles County single-family home, from contract signing to final inspection?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homeowners in Los Angeles County often underestimate the total timeline for a medium-sized window replacement project. After you sign a contract, the installer typically schedules a detailed measure appointment. Permits, if required, may take a few days to a few weeks depending on your city and whether plans must be reviewed for egress or exterior changes. Once measurements are finalized, windows are ordered. Custom-sized, energy-efficient units commonly used in the region can take roughly three to six weeks to manufacture and ship, sometimes longer during peak seasons. Installation of 10–20 windows usually spans one to three days, depending on accessibility, stucco or siding conditions, and whether full-frame work is needed. After installation, a city inspection may be required. Scheduling can add another few days to a week or more, depending on inspector availability. Allow additional time for minor touch-ups: paint, stucco patch curing, caulking, and screen adjustments. When planning, ask your contractor for a written timeline that breaks down measurement, permitting, ordering, installation, and inspection. Build in buffer time if you have trip plans, HOA review, or other renovation trades scheduled, so overlapping work does not slow the project.
acceptedAnswer.description: A realistic timeline to replace 10–20 windows in a Los Angeles County home is often 4–10 weeks from contract to final inspection: 1–3 weeks for permitting and measurements, 3–6 weeks for window manufacturing and delivery, and 1–3 days for installation plus a few days to schedule inspections and touch-ups.
